query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a cryogenic rolling deformation followed by an optimized low-temperature annealing treatment to a cast eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) will refine its lamellar dual-phase microstructure and activate additional deformation modes (e.g., increased twinning and dislocation interactions) that jointly improve yield strength and ductility relative to conventional processing.
generation.material_initial_state: A cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with an inherent dual-phase lamellar microstructure consisting of a soft FCC phase and a hard BCC (or intermetallic) phase, produced via standard casting and room-temperature thermo-mechanical processing.
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to cryogenic rolling (e.g., at liquid nitrogen temperature with approximately 50% thickness reduction) immediately followed by an annealing treatment at a temperature below the full recrystallization range to stabilize the refined microstructure.
generation.conditions: The intervention should be carried out under cryogenic deformation conditions with controlled strain rate, and the subsequent annealing should be precisely timed to retain ultrafine grains and enhanced twin density without allowing excessive grain coarsening.
generation.structural_mediator: An ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with a higher density of deformation twins and refined lamellar interfaces between the soft FCC and hard BCC (or associated intermetallic) phases.
generation.mechanism: Cryogenic rolling suppresses recovery and promotes a high dislocation density along with active nano-twinning, while the tailored annealing step stabilizes this refined structure. The enhanced twin and dislocation networks act as additional barriers to dislocation motion (two-hierarchical constraint effect) and aid in dissipating stress concentrations, thereby increasing both the yield strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to a baseline alloy processed via conventional room-temperature rolling and annealing, the treated alloy is expected to exhibit a statistically significant increase in yield strength and an improvement in tensile ductility. Although the precise percentage increase is uncertain, the simultaneous enhancement of these properties is anticipated due to the improved work-hardening capacity and microcrack arresting behavior.
generation.baseline: Conventionally processed eutectic HEAs (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) produced by standard casting followed by room-temperature rolling and annealing, which typically display a coarser lamellar microstructure with lower twin density.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are predicted as long as the rolling reduction and annealing temperature/time are optimized to avoid over-processing. If the reduction is too high or annealing too aggressive, the refined structure may coarsen or embrittle, negating the intended improvements.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the improvement in strength and ductility is not known and may depend sensitively on processing parameters such as the degree of deformation, cryogenic temperature uniformity, and annealing schedule.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples of the selected eutectic HEA. Process one set via cryogenic rolling (targeting ~50% thickness reduction at liquid nitrogen temperature) followed by an optimized low-temperature annealing treatment; process the other set via conventional room-temperature rolling and annealing. Conduct uniaxial tensile tests on both sets under identical conditions and use electron or optical microscopy to quantify the microstructural differences (e.g., grain size, twin density, and lamellar interface refinement).
measurements: Microstructural features (grain size, twin density, phase distribution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the cryogenically processed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in both yield strength and ductility, or if microstructural analysis fails to reveal the expected ultrafine structure with enhanced twin formation relative to the control, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Realizing improved strength–ductility synergy in eutectic alloys acting as in situ composite materials remains a challenge in conventional eutectic systems, which is why eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), a newly-emerging multi-principal-element eutectic category, may offer wider in situ composite possibilities. Here, we use an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that deliberately inherits its composite lamellar nature by tailored thermo-mechanical processing to achieve property combinations which are not accessible to previously-reported reinforcement methodologies. The as-prepared samples exhibit hierarchically-structural heterogeneity due to phase decomposition, and the improved mechanical response during deformation is attributed to both a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism. This work provides a pathway for strengthening eutectic alloys and widens the design toolbox for high-performance materials based upon EHEAs. To tackle the aforementioned problems, eutectic HEAs (EHEAs) [] were proposed. On the one hand, EHEAs should have the general character of traditional eutectic alloys. In this sense, EHEAs should have better fluidity and thus better castability and less casting defects [,]. On the other hand, EHEAs as one kind of in-situ composites with lamellar or rod-like eutectic microstructures might reach the balance between strength and ductility via mixing the soft FCC phase with the hard BCC phase or intermetallic compound [,,,,,,,,]. Some EHEAs indeed have outstanding properties. Lu et al. [] reported the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA with simultaneous high strength (944 MPa) and good ductility (25.6%). The excellent mechanical properties do not depend significantly on derivation of eutectic compositions []. After cold-rolling and annealing, its strength reached up to 1.2 GPa and its elongation could remain at about 12% []. After cryo-rolling and annealing, its strength could reach up to 1.47 GPa while its ductility could even increase to 14% []. He et al. [,] designed the CoCrFeNiNbx EHEAs and found that the microstructures were stable from 600 °C to 900 °C.
